challengeTypes: identify: What does the environment consist of? (Living and non-living things that interact vs Only living things | Only non-living things | Only plants)

sort: Drag each component to living or non-living (Plants = Living | Animals = Living | Air = Non-living | Water = Non-living | Humans = Living | Soil = Non-living | Sunlight = Non-living | Microbes = Living)
identify: Which of these is a SIMILARITY between plants and animals? (Both are living things vs Both can move around | Both make their own food | Both have a heart)

sort: Drag each feature to plant or animal (Makes own food by photosynthesis = Plant | Can move from place to place = Animal | Has roots, stem, leaves = Plant | Has organs like heart, lungs = Animal | Responds to stimuli = Both | Needs food and water = Both | Has chlorophyll = Plant | Has a nervous system = Animal)
identify: Which internal organ pumps blood to the whole body? (Heart vs Lungs vs Stomach vs Brain)

sort: Drag each organ to its correct function (Lungs = breathing, take in oxygen | Heart = pumps blood to whole body | Stomach = digests food | Brain = controls all body functions | Lungs = exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide | Stomach = breaks down food with acids)
identify: What is a PLAIN? (A flat area of land with grass vs A high mountain | A dry sandy area | A low area between mountains)

sort: Drag each physical feature to its correct description (Hills = raised areas lower than mountains | Plains = flat areas good for farming | Deserts = dry sandy areas with little rain | Valleys = low areas between mountains or hills | Mountains = highest landforms with peaks | Plateaus = flat raised areas)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Environment — everything around us, including living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) things that interact. Living: plants, animals, humans, microbes. Non-living: air, water, soil, sunlight. They depend on each other — plants need sunlight and water, animals need plants for food, humans need both. (2) Plants vs animals — Similarities: both are living, both grow, both need food and water, both reproduce, both respond to stimuli. Differences: Plants make their own food (photosynthesis), cannot move, have roots/stem/leaves, have chlorophyll. Animals cannot make food, can move, have organs (heart, lungs, brain), have nervous system. (3) Internal organs — Lungs: breathing, take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide. Heart: pumps blood to whole body, beats continuously. Stomach: digests food using acids and enzymes. Brain: controls all body functions and thinking. (4) Physical features — Hills: raised areas of land, lower than mountains. Plains: flat areas of land, good for farming and living. Deserts: dry sandy areas with very little rain, hot days and cold nights. Valleys: low areas between mountains or hills, often have rivers. Mountains: highest landforms with peaks. Plateaus: flat raised areas. Misconceptions: 'the environment is only about plants and animals' (WRONG — the environment includes both living and non-living things: air, water, soil, sunlight are also part of the environment), 'plants and animals have nothing in common' (WRONG — both are living, both grow, both need food and water, both reproduce, both respond to stimuli), 'the stomach pumps blood' (WRONG — the heart pumps blood; the stomach digests food), 'plains and plateaus are the same' (WRONG — plains are flat areas at LOW elevation; plateaus are flat areas at HIGH elevation), 'deserts have no life' (WRONG — deserts have adapted plants like cactus and animals like camels, snakes, and lizards).
